short: The most famous British fighter of the Second World War, critical to victory in the Battle of Britain.
full:
Designed by R.J. Mitchell, the Supermarine Spitfire was an advanced single-seat fighter that combined an elliptical wing with the powerful Rolls-Royce Merlin engine. Entering service in 1938, it became a symbol of British defiance during the summer of 1940 when it was pitted against the Luftwaffe in the Battle of Britain. Although the Hawker Hurricane shot down more aircraft during the campaign, the Spitfire's superior high-altitude performance made it the primary interceptor against German fighters.

The Spitfire was the only Allied fighter to be manufactured in continuous production before, during, and after the Second World War, with over twenty thousand built. Successive variants incorporated larger engines, reinforced airframes, and heavier armament to keep pace with rapid wartime aeronautical development. It served in every theatre of the conflict and remained in front-line service with foreign air forces well into the 1950s.
